To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

2,6-diamino purines are CDK inhibitors, that CDK2 inhibitors can be developed by iterating chemical libraries with biological screening, that the crystal structures of CDK2-purine complexes reveal the basis for binding affinity and selectivitiy, and that the cellular effects of CDK inhibitors can be characterized by monitoring changes in the levels of messenger RNA with high density oligonucleotide array analysis.
